Length can disclose a shared secret

In the synthetic Heron security lab, a response combines an attacker-controlled string with a secret value and compresses them together. Repeated guesses can change the compressed length when a guess shares a prefix with the secret. Encryption of the resulting bytes does not necessarily hide their length. The lab separates secret content from attacker-controlled compression contexts. It does not claim that disabling compression solves every side channel; timing and cache behavior require separate review.
